shortDescription: Shares of India's Shriram Finance NSE:SHRIRAMFIN fell to an 11-month low on Monday after the non-bank lender lowered its annual loan growth forecast and warned of higher credit costs, overshadowing a better-than-expected second-quarter profit.Shares fell as much as 6.13% to 810.20 rupees, extending…

children: fell to an 11-month low on Monday after the non-bank lender lowered its annual loan growth forecast and warned of higher credit costs, overshadowing a better-than-expected second-quarter profit.
Shares fell as much as 6.13% to 810.20 rupees, extending losses from Friday, and were on track for an eighth consecutive session of declines.

The company cut its assets under management growth forecast for fiscal 2027 to 15%-17% from 18%, citing weak monsoon conditions and geopolitical uncertainty, and flagged pressure on borrowers in drought-hit regions.

Jefferies said credit costs could remain elevated for another one to two quarters as stress rises in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Telangana. The brokerage maintained its "buy" rating but cut its target price to 1,145 rupees from 1,210 rupees.
Higher slippages and write-offs reflected drought-like conditions in several states, Motilal Oswal said, adding that the lender's overall asset quality remained broadly stable.

JM Financial said rising early-stage delinquencies and drought-related stress among rural borrowers remained key concerns for Shriram Finance. The brokerage maintained its "buy" rating but cut its target price to 1,025 rupees from 1,175 rupees, citing deteriorating asset quality indicators.

Shriram Finance reported a nearly 60% jump in second-quarter profit to 36.77 billion rupees ($387.30 million) on Friday, beating analysts' estimate of 35.46 billion rupees, according to LSEG-compiled data.
